I own an Asus Rog Flow X13 with a `04f3:0c6e Elan Microelectronics Corp. ELAN:Fingerprint`
fingerprint reader, which currently does not work on Linux[^not-working].

In this blog post, we dive into how we can fix this ourselfes by reverse 
engineering the fingerprint reader and adding appropriate support to
`libfprint`.

## Project setup

I use NixOS ([read more about this here](../nixos-git-analysis/)), a Linux 
distribution with the pleasent benefit that you (the reader) can simply run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/quoteme/libfprint.git
cd libfprint
nix develop
```

to enter a completely reproducible development environment with all dependencies
installed, perfectly fit for following this guide.

I decided to try [Flake Parts](https://flake.parts/) this time around. Without 
diving too much into why, the reason being that it hopefully makes the
development shell easier to extend for _your_ future Linux driver.
